caveats: This independently adopted stepped-rock design replaces the legacy spiral-body design only in this direction set. All 16 images are newly generated; legacy root images and metadata remain unchanged and were not image references.

One continuous monolithic rock has a broad lower block and centered half-width upper extension, two short rectangular feet, one eye on the upper front, no arms, wings or tail. The upper and lower portions share front/back endpoints; shoulders extend sideways. Side views hide the shoulders in depth and the far foot behind the near foot.

Front and front-diagonal views show the single eye; side and rear views show no eye. Oblique views connect the stepped front/back plane to the unmarked side plane. W and E are nearly symmetric unmarked sides; their unique orientation cannot be proved from outline alone.

A broad blue-gray lower-body stratum has a thin pale-yellow stratum immediately above it. The adopted baseline renders these two distinguishable layers adjacent rather than with a visible taupe gap. This difference from the wording slightly above remains recorded.
Palette roles are taupe rock and feet #C7A18A, broad layer #879BAA and thin layer #EBDEA4, with lighting and granular material shades.
Exact depth ratios, 45-degree yaw intervals, camera elevation, rigid stone-grain rotation and hidden shoulder/foot connections are artistic approximations, not measured 3D proof.
Direction-specific fitting makes W/E appear taller than the broad front/back views at their individual canvas scale. Common world-scale runtime rendering is untested.

Each selected pixel image uses its same-direction normal as the sole image reference. Pixel art simplifies rounded corners, eye highlights and stone grain; yellow eye-rim shifts, stronger diagonal grain and stepped layer boundaries remain visible.
W and SW each retain an earlier rejected normal separately; neither rejected image is part of this set. Structure diagrams were private production aids and are not delivered assets.
Reference arrays and hashes were recorded before reference-based calls and checked locally with returned outputs. No separate service-side input digest was provided.
